title: Locust Year
logline: A Choptank planter gives his estate to his brother, rides with the Methodists, and vows not to lie down all winter.

title: Uncle No
logline: A Little Saigon miser who hammered his son's earrings himself won't pay for a doctor when the boy's eyes turn yellow.

title: No Winters
logline: In an Arctic roadhouse where a man's age is his winters, a stout newcomer takes the old-timers' chair and will not get up.

title: Dinner on the Ground
logline: In the Ozark drought, a young mother whose first two babies died flees with her third into a girl preacher's brush arbor.

title: The Washing Cup
logline: On a Catskills dairy hill, a basin of standing water splits a Jewish farm colony, and the old rav walks into the woods.

title: The Cooling Board
logline: A Kentucky hog drover joins the Shakers and sits nightly in their burying ground; his younger brother follows, meaning to bring him home.

title: Four Votes
logline: After a Ramadan feast for a thousand, a Bosnian congregation votes on who should wear a judge's hundred-year-old fur-lined cloak.

title: Heart and Sap
logline: Two friends from Eleuthera sign with a pirate captain at Nassau to learn what keeps, and ask the question in every port for a year and a half.

title: Beat In the Reed
logline: A Kentish thatcher follows his cousin's communion cup from his own wedding onto a Virginia ship, and every roof he lays there leaks.

title: The Slats
logline: In the swine-flu autumn, Dutch Reformed farmers on an Iowa gravel road hear hogs screaming from a cruel neighbor's house every night.

title: The Izote
logline: In the Maryland suburbs, a dying Salvadoran drywaller whose fourteen children keep sixteen kinds of giving asks the church to read him one chapter.

title: Horseshoe Lake
place: Bevo Mill and Carondelet Park, St. Louis, Missouri
logline: Passed over by his Bosnian congregation, a mosque volunteer attaches himself to a trucking heir and asks the old imam to step aside.

title: Little Brother
logline: In Moravian Salem, where the Lot decides who marries, a tavern keeper's dying youngest daughter calls him by a name he cannot understand.

title: The Third Chair
place: Gorham and North Haverhill, New Hampshire
logline: A police chief's Seneca table sends one friend to milk another man's cows and the other to half a million subscribers.

title: Castile Roses
place: Santa Cruz de la Cañada, New Mexico
logline: In Spanish New Mexico, a jealous third wife plots against the women who watch a genízaro hermit through holes in their walls.

title: Paid in Rice
logline: A bearded woodsman calls the Jews of Charles Town to prayer each dawn, and a blind old merchant hears money in his voice.

title: Little Wayland
logline: A boy who can't hold four lines of scripture, a white handkerchief, and a pecan grove full of himself.

title: Folding Chairs
logline: During the worst week of spring break, retired garment workers on A1A keep their blind Dante teacher indoors and wait out the noise.

title: The Counting Tower
logline: A Yup'ik church helper hired to count salmon ten minutes an hour decides to count every living thing that comes and goes.

title: Neither Cold Nor Hot
logline: In the gas-shortage winter of 1977, two Methodist friends at a suburban Ohio engineering firm are told to get up early and watch.

title: Caliche
logline: At a border truck-yard gate, a taco seller tells a customs broker's daughter how a transfer driver with a shovel came to run heaven.

title: The Closed Cone
logline: A seminary dropout working as a Yellowstone seasonal ranger can make nothing of the pinecone his teacher gave him, until the summer the park burns.

title: Salt Tea
logline: A young Kalmyk monk eats only what the refugee houses on his road can spare, while a rich patron feasts the lamas in Philadelphia.

title: Julie Mango
logline: A young man who carries a pandita's harmonium begs leave to go and meditate alone in an old mango grove by a canal.

title: The Dinner Bell
logline: Sixty followers of a pandemic nurse's one-minute videos spend the monsoon at a widow's empty RV park on the Verde River.

title: Clear Hands
logline: A builder's son does everything the fighting-game scene asks of him, in order, until a team house leaves him no room to move his hands.

title: Three Shirts
logline: Back from a summer running a Door County drive-in, a young projectionist brings his uncle a wool shirt the uncle will not take.

title: The Weathervane
logline: A Harlem stride pianist joins Father Divine's Sayville household for the food, goes home to his wife, and comes back, six times.

title: The Water Pot
logline: Four Washington meditators sent to sit three months in an old Catholic novitiate find the woods around it already occupied.

title: Hot Water
logline: During the 1973 grape strike, old Filipino farmworkers carry their festering housemate out under the pepper tree, and their quietest man lights the stove.

title: Blaze Orange
logline: A Wisconsin dairyman feeds an old Hmong elder for seven days, then walks him down the lane on the opening morning of deer season.

title: The Midwife's Driver
logline: A rich Czech son in Chicago looks at a midwife washing in the river the way he looks at everything, and his body changes.

title: The Stone Crop
logline: After the summer that never came, a Vermont company walks to Ohio arguing soils, carrying an old widow and a book about heaven.

title: Notional Water
logline: An Iraqi-born Army medic training in a fake Iraqi town in the Mojave takes clay prayer beads from the old refugee who plays its tea seller.

title: Thin Shade
logline: A proud ranching family scrubs the chair a judge's son sat in, and an old curandera sits in the road.

title: Since Morning
logline: On the Fraser, a Hawaiian sealer's wife keeps a plank chapel, praying with every offering to get back to her husband.

title: Seven Doors
logline: Two days after the chicken-plant raids, a Guatemalan landlord locks seven doors to eat one bean cake unseen, and an old man appears outside the window.

title: The Limbertwig
logline: In a secret city's trailer camp, a calutron operator asks the bathhouse woman to dinner against the wishes of the young preacher she feeds.

title: Besobila
logline: The summer the Derg falls, a night cashier keeps his seat on a nun's basement floor when an exiled governor walks in.

title: Yesterday’s Bread
logline: A Toledo bride who walked through the rain marries into the Southend's richest house and tells her father-in-law what he's eating.

title: The Contrary Wind
logline: On the first voyage west, a ship's boy who airs the Admiral's spice box asks the old steward whether any smell travels to windward.

title: Slippery Dumplings
logline: An old Catholic Worker will eat only what the poorest give him, and a fading chemical heir means to be the poorest.

title: The Yellow Fiddle
logline: At a new Trappist house in the Ozarks, an old lay brother nurses a young Marine whose malaria keeps coming back.

title: Pond Lilies
logline: Two old friends on Cape Cod, one a Baptist and one taken with traveling mediums, trade a ruined supper for a clambake over a pit of fire.

title: Stay Time
logline: A Hanford manager wants his driver's wife and sends him upriver for red clay and blue lilies. That night four sounds cross the desert.

title: Swallow Mud
place: Shin Pond road near Patten, Maine
logline: Past the closed paper mills, an old Heathen priest takes in two young men, and one keeps telling him his bath is ready.

title: Five Places
logline: In the season when the dead come home hungry, an unlucky boy walks into a rich man's house as if he knows it.

title: Welcome to Our Table
logline: Two runaway apprentices who pick pockets under the hill at Natchez slip aboard a floating theatre; only one of them remembers to steal.

title: The Iron Ladle
place: Upper West Side, Manhattan, New York
logline: Three young cooks ride uptown to learn from the master of Hunan cooking and find a smiling old man in the chef's chair.

title: The Silk-Cotton Trees
logline: On Saint Martin's day 1510, thirty young hidalgos chase a Taíno woman who took their gold, and meet a friar under the ceibas.

title: The Blue Cup
logline: A Norwegian leper who eats off his own tin plate stands outside a barn door to hear a woman preach.

title: Snake in the Furrow
place: Roxborough Township and the Wissahickon, Pennsylvania
logline: An Irish tenant plowing the Ridge above the Wissahickon hears an old hermit say there is a snake at the corner of his field.

title: The Roof Walk
logline: A Black gardener carrying a whaling captain's morning roses up County Street meets the old Gay Head harpooneer who meets every ship.

title: Honey on the Knife
place: Centreville and the Page Valley, Virginia
logline: A Korean American nun living alone in a Shenandoah Valley cabin is betrayed by the cousin who has wanted her since childhood.

title: The Sedge Straw
logline: A hookworm dispensary's young microscopist asks a night's lodging of the man the Mountain feeds from a sedge straw, who claims to eat wind.

title: Banked Fire
logline: The morning after the Dutch burn San Juan, an old soldier looks down the length of the smoking town and smiles.

title: A Thousand Stamps
logline: Carrying the Christmas oak down past the Homestake mills, a Montenegrin timberman stops, looks at the thousand stamps, and smiles.

title: Sesame Cake
place: Bloomington, Indiana, and Mount Shasta, California
logline: Asked last to a supper at an Indiana natural-foods store, the man who runs its meditation group insults the host and boards a Greyhound.

title: The Heavenly Road
logline: In the first spring of freedom on St. Helena Island, a seven-year-old seeker gives away a thousand blankets and goes where kin cannot follow.

title: Reading Glasses
logline: A retired Navy steward of sixty-seven mops the stage of a Norfolk drag bar and asks, once, to be put in the show.

title: Lilac Slips
logline: Two young Methodist exhorters plant lilacs around a mill-settlement schoolhouse, and an old class leader sends her right hand and her left.

title: Fourth Day
logline: A pastor's old groom, who rode with him the night he fled England, cannot forgive the two men his master now leans on.

title: The Placemat
logline: A Greek diner king who has searched for years hears from a produce driver that an elder has come, and gives away a diner per word.

title: Four Redfish
logline: A seven-year-old Bronzeville seeker, heir to a family legend of silver rain, watches three tradesmen at work and turns back alone.

title: Zio Nino
logline: In a Barre granite shed, apprentices stand a four-foot anarchist carver on a block each noon and pinch his nose shut, and he waits.

title: Kaneez’s Mother
logline: Four times a widow in Queens fries malpure for her daughter's in-laws, and four times the doorbell rings.

title: Struck Measure
logline: A Mien grandmother brings her mushroom crew to the Oregon pine for a buyer who forgets them, in a fall when nothing comes up.

title: Decay Heat
logline: An engineer hired to watch a nuclear control room and touch nothing tells his wife, over coffee, that he wants to leave the world.

title: Hands Full
logline: Forty-one neighbors on one street of a desert city vow to stand through a DJ's whole set, from sundown to sunrise.

title: White City
logline: When the freeze stops the threshing, fifty harvest hands ride into a hobo jungle to see the man who keeps its cans clean.

title: Cedar Bark
logline: The morning of an atomic test, a Dixie doctor is kept from getting back to unbind an old patriarch's wounded foot.

title: Castle Rock
logline: As Tule Lake empties in 1946, a coal-crew man washes his clothes while the others pack, and the camp decides he will never leave.

title: Sukhari
logline: After the heat dome, a Ukrainian baker in a Portland tent village dries bakery bread on a shower roof and shuts himself in to pray.

title: Three Hems
logline: On trash-day mornings a Burmese teenager walks the alleys with an old monk who will wear only what Fort Wayne throws away.

title: The Slow Ascent
logline: An old Kalymnian sponge diver who never once came up too fast writes that he cannot come to Tarpon Springs for the Epiphany.

title: The Doorsill
logline: A Rusyn first sergeant who says every draftee's name right misses one, and the boy swears the sergeant struck him.

title: One Hand
place: Smithtown Branch, Long Island, New York
logline: On occupied Long Island a schoolmaster who carries letters for a spy line takes a deacon's seven-year-old son as his boy, and sleeps through his watch.

title: The Demon Star
logline: At a Vermont academy's public examination, a teacher asks her assistant whether she believes what the class has just recited about a star.

title: Uña de Gato
logline: Betrothed at seven by a silver widow who has lost six children to the Church, her last son slips out of the coach on the road home.

title: The Bell Pool
logline: A warehouse picker sits nine days beside a ruined honeymoon resort's pool, until a woman stood up by a client finds him there.

title: Copper Teeth
logline: The colony's hangman, dismissed in his sixties, cooks the last of the King's rice and milk, and someone knocks at his door.

title: The King’s Bowl
logline: A castaway in birch bark is fed all winter as a saint at the Straits, until a drowned friend appears over the ice.

title: The Branch
logline: A berry farmer's daughter marries the copper thief her father bought out of prison, and he asks her to climb a mountain.

title: Watering Off
logline: The spring after the great flood, a professional horseplayer asks an old hot walker at Churchill Downs whether he knows anything about losing.

title: Each Halting Place
logline: A Fremont flooring man who has sent a thousand dollars a month for twenty-two years rides to a desert detention center with his nephew.

title: The Ring Seal
place: Upton and Riverhead, Long Island, New York
logline: A young technician who raises a radiation source over a dying forest each noon is sent to watch his uncle work glass.

title: Another Man's Hat
place: San Miguel del Vado, New Mexico
logline: At a Santa Fe Trail ford, the rich man who arranges the customs duties spends a year paying for his saint's feast.

title: From Its Stem
logline: An Extension worker borrows sixteen folding chairs so the old people of a refugee garden can chant for seven days around a five-year-old.

title: Thirty Nobles
logline: Thirty old Shriners building a lake camp for burned children are told to take along a seven-year-old found alive in the ashes.

title: The Window Dummy
logline: On the night of the 1977 blackout, looters stack a store's worth of goods around a figure in a stripped Broadway show window.

title: The Second Razor
logline: The barber-porter on the Overland Limited offers to throw a rattlesnake off the train, and that night cuts the crew's hair with two razors.

title: Spilt Water
logline: A rich man's daughter runs off with his truck driver, and years later walks home along the lake as a hurricane comes in.

title: The Mustard Seed
logline: In the influenza autumn, a young mother goes door to door for a seed from a house where no one has died.

title: Tree Prayer
logline: A widow who ran a cleaners on Candler Road for thirty-four years gives everything to her seven children, then moves through their guest rooms.

title: One Shawl
place: Great Salt Lake City, Utah Territory
logline: In the hungry autumn of the handcart rescue, a Welsh quarryman sits all night in a bishop's yard wearing his household's only shawl.

title: The Recall Card
logline: A hockey dad selling pull-tabs for the Boosters in a suburban bar starts playing his own box, until his dental hygienist sends for him.

title: The Fanner
logline: On a Sea Island plantation the masters have fled, a refugee girl minding ricebirds gives a praise-house elder her whole skillet of parched rice.

title: Going-Home Money
logline: After the April Fool's tsunami takes his buried savings, a Chinese storekeeper keeps carrying jook up the hill to a blinded veteran.

title: A Trace
logline: The best lifeguard at a suburban swim club leaves sixty chaise lounges out every night, until the board president hands her his rain gauge.

title: Three Fingers
logline: After Hurricane Laura a school bus driver asks a wrecked rice town to feed the cooks who fed it, and the dryer owner gives a pinch.

title: Grindstone Ford
logline: A Pittsburgh merchant with four kegs of Spanish dollars and twelve broke boatmen reaches the last house before the Choctaw wilderness.

title: A Whole Hand
place: Philadelphia and the New Jersey Pine Barrens
logline: A merchant's daughter who has sworn off meat follows a Pine Barrens deer hunter home from the Jersey Market and runs his bullets for twenty-eight years.

title: The Mantle
logline: A fur hunter who blames a young monk for his empty day sets his Kamchatka bear dogs on him in the spruce.

title: The Cleaning Table
logline: On a Friday in Lent, a Minnesota jeweler on a Cape Coral canal sets a car dealer's natural pearl down on his fish-cleaning table.

title: A Jar of Sand
logline: Three parties of Chilean forty-niners, by road, by sea and out of a sealed cave, bring what they saw to an old man who weighs gold.

title: The Seventh Floor
logline: In Prohibition Butte, a department-store king blocks his son-in-law's path in the street, and hears what the doctor says about it.

title: The Parking Chair
logline: After the 1993 blizzard, seventeen young renters dig out a curb in a Pittsburgh streetcar suburb, and six longtime neighbors come to take it.

title: Rule Two
logline: A Palouse farm wife whose son is in Vietnam drives the school bus, where six older boys want the back seat seventeen children scrubbed clean.

title: Bull Snake
logline: Two months after Oklahoma City, eleven militia boys on a Salmon River bar corner a snake they are sure is a rattler.

title: Two Coffees
logline: At a megachurch in an old Walmart, everyone sees a teenage girl following the new youth pastor except the youth pastor.

title: A to Izzard
logline: On Fast Day the squire's wife asks the women of a hill town what each is fasting for, while a drove of fat oxen goes by.

title: Four Hundredweight
logline: A Catholic planter who prices a sleeping stranger as a runaway loses his tobacco, his cattle and then the mass room he loves.

title: Piedra Negra
logline: Rival spirit-sellers pay five boys a thousand dollars to kill the old medium at Piedra Negra, who visits the dead for free.

title: Sin Vergüenza
logline: A widowed water commissioner goes to live with the Rainbow Family and own nothing, and brings a motorhome, a freezer and two paid cooks.

title: Seven Palms
logline: During the King's jubilee, a decorated cowboy-deputy rides past his old schoolteacher without getting off his horse.

title: The Sugar Sack
logline: A beet-field boy who rode the freights joins the CCC at an Army horse depot and hangs his sugar-sack shirt in a cottonwood.

title: The Long Day
place: Sacaton, Gila River Indian Reservation, Arizona
logline: In the dry summer after the Coolidge Dam, a seven-year-old Pima boy watches men lead water, straighten arrows and iron a wheel.

title: The Oakum Loft
logline: In Christmas week the caulkers' wives climb to an old man's night school with jugs under their cloaks, and he puts out the lamp.

title: What Shall I Cry
logline: A young friar falls in love with a famous beauty he has never seen, from one old friar's talk at supper.

title: The Hem
logline: In Guam's hungry year, a Chamorro woman older than the mission gives the food from her prayer rounds to a thin choirboy three days running.

title: The Night Board
logline: Five young farmers come home from a revival fast sure the flesh is dead in them. The night operator sends them to the dead.

title: Outward Adorning
logline: A coalfield beauty queen follows her whole family into the Holiness church for love, not faith, and hides from her preacher brother's sermons.

title: One Shot
logline: A lowrider club president sees his wife on the wash-bay camera, believes her story about it, and later asks a pinstriper where she is.

title: Sixteen Oxen
place: Clay Hill (fictional), Merrimack County, New Hampshire
logline: An old Grange chaplain reads funeral scripture at weddings; his auctioneer son remembers teaching him to ask a rich man for one ox.

title: Third Sunrise
place: Low Earth orbit and Clear Lake (Houston), Texas
logline: A spacewalker is left hanging on a stalled robot arm through three orbital nights, and at the third sunrise says something Houston cannot place.

title: The Lily Pond
logline: A Hartford boy taught nothing but singing marries a girl taught nothing but dancing, and four men wait on a fence for his car.

title: One Watch
logline: A Banks boy turned Wall Street millionaire builds a lodge that seems to float, then plots against the carpenter who could build another.

title: The Middle Portion
logline: A Greek preacher with a famous voice shops four railroad towns for the best Lenten fee, then stops to divide a dead man's things.

title: The Gravedigger's Rooster
logline: At a suburban synagogue's first all-night Shavuot study, the chairman who organized it keeps slipping into the rabbi's study to check a source.

title: Mataji
logline: A Phoenix debutante joins the Hare Krishnas without knowing she is pregnant, and must prove her vows before the temple turns her out.

title: The Imposing Stone
logline: A Mississippi wood hauler who cannot read sits up every press night in a Springfield printing office to hear the proofs read aloud.

title: Strangler Fig
logline: On a shell-mound key in the plume-hunting years, a bird warden's wife digs a splinter from his foot while the porch talks about his cousin.

title: Porch Lights
logline: In Halley's Comet winter, a letter carrier goes door to door on a cul-de-sac asking fourteen houses to turn off their porch lights.

title: The Nooning
logline: A deaf widow's only sermon is the few words her boarder writes on a slate, until a girl comes home from Hartford signing.

title: Windmill Water
logline: A carbon-black hand walks out of an all-night Salvation Army prayer meeting in an oil boomtown, and a payroll sack lands at his feet.

title: Spiritual Bouquet
logline: While his parish heaps prayers and flowers on a dying Jesuit, a Purina feed salesman takes a motel room by the week.

title: Cistern Water
place: Frederiksted, St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands
logline: A month after Hurricane Hugo, a girl straining cistern water laughs at her own reflection, and a young Rasta laughs with her.

title: Better Than Sleep
logline: A banquet-hall owner sets six hundred chairs for his son the shaykh, who is out before dawn with a drum, waking the cul-de-sacs.

title: Homo Bulla
logline: In the missile week of October 1962, five Latin students who cannot translate thirteen lines on death go to ask their teacher for Caesar.

title: Dead Air
logline: The program log of a Nevada radio station for the week a wounded lieutenant is king of the bond drive, and the night after.

title: The Push Broom
logline: A retired shop teacher who cannot stop sweeping a Quaker meetinghouse is told by an old man to go wash up and sit down.

title: Stand Still
logline: A bushwhacker with a string of fingers around his neck chases an old Dunkard he can't catch.

title: The Quills
logline: In Silk City, a weaver's daughter winds her father's quills for three years, repeating what an old Bundist once told a memorial meeting.

title: By What Road
place: Little Creek Hundred, Kent County, Delaware
logline: Thirty people walk out of a Delaware salt marsh before dawn, and a Quaker boy waits at the gate with a hay wagon.

title: Only You and I
logline: Rival pastors put a church soloist in a red coat up to ruining the Haitian layman who fills out everyone's forms for free.

title: The Sopas
logline: In a record milk year, the richest Azorean dairyman in Valeta keeps losing the Holy Ghost festa's giving contest to everyone else.

title: The Luminaria
logline: A plate-lunch cook who feeds half of Sarpy County pays his sneaker-reselling son to stay all night at the Relay For Life.

title: One Footprint
logline: A Telugu engineer who has refused every suitor for his daughter offers her to a thin stranger watching his sunrise fire.

title: Three Ladders
logline: A policy banker hangs a mahogany bowl ninety feet over Lenox Avenue and dares Harlem's holy men to fly up and take it.

title: Water Coconut
logline: A Catholic woman who logs the shrimp fleet's radio writes down the night a captain's daughter sang her riddle and a deckhand answered.

title: The Souvenir Journal
logline: A church clerk who forgets nothing finds one thing missing from her fortieth-anniversary page of seven pastors, and asks the seventh.

title: A Hundred Eggs
place: Lakewood and Jackson Township, New Jersey
logline: A young scholar in the Lakewood kollel inherits eighteen hundred dollars from a chicken farmer and stops turning the pages.

title: The Sand Pile
logline: A coal company's retired preacher leads three hundred people up a mountain to wait out Y2K, where a rattlesnake takes their penance pile.

title: Sire and Dam
logline: On orphan-train day in an Iowa county seat, a herdsman who knows every pedigree but his own asks where good men come from.

title: Mic Check
logline: On the snowy night the generators are taken, twenty cold occupiers in the Zuccotti kitchen argue over the best thing in the world.

title: Summer Fallow
logline: Walking to a church blessing in the summer the colony split, an old Orthodox cantor stops at a priest's grave cross where a farmer is plowing.

title: Bean Bread
logline: In the dry summer after removal, two Cherokee sisters' families face each other with rifles across a mill dam on a dying creek.

title: Crowns on Their Heads
logline: On Halloween in the fenced atomic town, a machinist's daughter goes door to door while her father waits for a security hearing.

title: The Level
logline: After the Morgan affair, an old Mason judge loses the town election three springs running to the nephew he raised.

title: Strained Water
logline: At a Catholic wedding on the Port Tobacco River, the bride strains spring water for the old priests while the groom watches only her.

title: Loaf Mass
logline: A Wiccan priestess drives six hours to a Maine hayfield for one man, who has gone into the woods after his only ox.

title: The Last Course
logline: A coal baron who sleeps through his own life is handed a prescription to be read aloud at the last course of every dinner.

title: The Cure Chair
logline: In a tuberculosis cure cottage, a dying classics teacher has four months left, and one boarder stops coming down to hear her read.

title: Thousand Eyes
logline: A country star flies home from London to nurse the dying drag queen who once answered his question in a dressing room.

title: Empty-Handed
logline: A Long Island cooper and his wife follow their only son into a Dutch commune that seats husbands and wives at separate tables.

title: The Potato Ground
logline: After the great fire of 1871, a Belgian farmer walks every day to the potato patch where his son died, until the settlement's old reader comes up the track.

title: Eleven a Day
logline: On a cul-de-sac built over an apple orchard, a Baptist widow who keeps a room for missionaries crosses the circle at night to a Bell Labs statistician.

title: New Clothes
logline: On Lunar New Year in Little Taipei, an old classics teacher watches six rich Taiwanese boys in new silk drive off to a hillside pool.

title: Has She Arrived
logline: A Jain jeweler's son who wants no wife casts a woman in red gold, and two salesmen stand her on the Virginia Beach boardwalk.

title: Low Ground
logline: A Lumbee farmer clears his grandfather's old tobacco field for cotton, and every morning the mail carrier stops to ask what he's doing.

title: Fair Play
logline: On Mardi Gras under the Claiborne oaks, five hundred Sunday-school children carrying cakes walk past a grand marshal and his brass band.

title: White River
logline: The winter the sociologists came to Middletown, two holiness students ask an old Methodist preacher whether he has been made perfect.

title: Everlasting Cottages
place: Walnut Creek Township, Holmes County, Ohio
logline: A rich Amish pallet maker builds a winter cottage in Florida for his unpaid ministers, and an old harness-maker sees what rose with it.

title: Cowhage
logline: In Colorado’s 1904 mine wars, a mine owner’s daughter hidden behind a veil sells her mother’s diamonds and sweeps under a church going up.

title: Four Saplings
logline: A Jain grandmother keeps the game world on Peaceful, until a cousin takes an axe to the tree a mother and child live in.

title: The Red Umbrella
logline: A Cantonese laborer's plowed field turns to gold, and his daughter hires Marysville's most famous singing girl to buy herself a fortnight.

title: As If Living
logline: A freedman taking the 1870 census, the first to write his people by name, crosses Caney Creek to eleven houses that were never there.

title: Hot Dish
logline: In a drought fall, an old farm couple kneel on the highway shoulder and greet a Thai Rotary exchange student as their long-lost son.

title: Rice Water
logline: An undocumented caregiver grinds rice all night for a rich man's Christmas stall and sees lights climbing the stairs to the chapel.

title: The Touchstone
logline: During the Ninevite fast, a Chaldean car salesman livestreams three teachers to five hundred viewers and is angry at all of them.

title: The New Pane
logline: Six boys in wooden shoes play kolf down a frozen Dutch street during the catechism sermon, past an old glazier's window.

title: Neat’s Tongue
logline: A Puritan butcher’s son flees a judgment, spends forty years engraving death’s heads on Boston mourning rings, and is fetched home by his sons.

title: The Drop Corner
logline: A retired draftsman who used to phone in complaints about the paperboys on his corner sees a canvas bag drag through wet grass.

title: Seven Days on the Nail
logline: A young Finnish miner's sister unweaves his coarse homespun and makes him a fine coat, as the ground under their town gives way.

title: Rocks and Shoals
place: A fleet submarine on patrol west of the Marianas
logline: On a 1944 war patrol, a qualified torpedoman boasts he can teach the boat better than the chiefs, and the nonquals take him up on it.

title: The Backstaff
logline: A pardoned pirate who keeps his share buried hides from Nassau's waterfront when his young wife goes dancing without him.

title: Pond Mullet
logline: On a Kauai sugar plantation, a young Buddhist priest paid in choice food for forbidden cures offers a share to an old Okinawan weeder.

title: Odd and Even
logline: Stuck in a gas line on Colesville Road, five suburban commuters argue over whose one kept promise is the hardest.

title: A Peck a Head
logline: Fed on charity above the falls of the James, a young Huguenot reader finds fault with every sack of Indian meal.

title: Fire Year
logline: A fire captain from Santa Paula briefs five Ojai men at a ranch gate while the Thomas Fire comes over the ridge.

title: Seven Furrows
logline: A Panhandle family down to one pound of meal on Black Sunday; ninety years on, their heir goes to hear a young wheat cutter.

title: Best Construction
logline: After the October snow breaks every tree on a Lincoln cul-de-sac, the compliance chairman writes eleven notices, and every one is correct.

title: Hawk Weather
place: Below the Blue Mountain, Berks County, Pennsylvania
logline: A retired schoolmaster who has shot and mounted sixty-one hawks goes at last to put three questions to the pupil who flies.

title: Not of Record
logline: Five members of a library Great Books group duck out of the rain into a justice of the peace's Tuesday night court.

title: Hollow Gourd
logline: Six MCs from Kelly Street take every mic in the Bronx, and a Jamaican super who never touches the mic keeps the record going.

title: The Votum
logline: In the drought summer, an old Lutheran farmer who can say only one sentence since his stroke hosts two famous preachers at the Missionfest.

title: The Milk Crate
logline: Thirty Berlin techno pilgrims come to a Grand River record-and-book shop to meet the Old Man, and a small boy holds the door.

title: Devil Grass
logline: In the Douglas drafting room the year the DC-8 entered service, two senior draftsmen with beautiful lettering ask the chief for a new rule.

title: Seven O'Clock
logline: A shaved-headed campus atheist with a YouTube channel wins every debate in Ellis County, one way or another.

title: Brother Fly
logline: A Paris beggar shipped to Louisiana in chains tells an old Capuchin with an alms sack that they are in the same trade.

title: The Pickle Stone
logline: In a small Zen temple, the kitchen women feed two kinds of Americans: one talks too much, and one never says thank you.

title: The Stringer
logline: On a hot Sunday on Belle Isle, a foundryman fishing for perch waits for an old schoolteacher to ask his name.

title: Six Bottles
logline: Six Denver Turners who have trained all summer tell their old gymnastics master that Longs Peak is as good as climbed.

title: The Road Book
logline: An Evanston wheel club talks of nothing but roads all summer, until the former racer who taught them to ride comes home.

title: Twenty Thousand Days
logline: Four lifers in the Castle on the Cumberland tell their monthly Sri Lankan monk that a year of meditation hasn't worked.

title: Twelve Stacks
logline: Eighteen retired Mon Valley workers lie on a library floor for eight weeks in a back-pain study, and their pain does not budge.

title: The Mourner's Bench
logline: A Kansas Holiness boy who never could pray the self to death takes a capsule in a chapel basement on Good Friday.

title: The Tin Horn
logline: At a Tennessee camp meeting, forty young men come out of the woods converted, and the one who went back to his wagon the first night means to catch up before morning.

title: The Dress Coat
logline: Two keepers who have shared a Maine ledge light for twenty years take a gifted new assistant around the island harbors to preach.

title: The Blue-Belly
place: Chicago and the hills past Mount Hamilton, California
logline: A Chicago Sanskrit scholar whom his swami greets as "empty Mr. Pottle" goes west to a ranch of meditators to be taught.

title: Sweet Root
logline: Five old Lao refugees who built a temple in the Louisiana cane become monks, and still eat every morning on one woman's porch.

title: Gold Leaf
logline: A Vietnam veteran from a family of U Street gold-leaf sign painters can't make his recovery counselor's method work.

title: Madder Red
place: Kilkenny, White Mountain National Forest, New Hampshire
logline: A Dead-lot tie-dye vendor with five hundred red shirts is stranded at a rainy Rainbow Gathering, where nobody uses money.

title: Dry Mustard
logline: A young mother on a three-year-old street goes door to door with a measuring cup, sure nobody has died in houses so new.

title: The Children's House
logline: After the hurricane of 1824, a nurse girl on a Georgia rice plantation throws mud at a bereaved woman the whole quarter wants gone.

title: Toussaint
place: Bayou Lafourche and Chênière Caminada, Louisiana
logline: After the October storm of 1893, the survivors of the Chênière send up the bayou for an old traiteuse who will not treat across water.

title: The Egg Chamber
logline: Ninety-five years after a bucket of turtle eggs, a mother runs down a dark Florida beach with her third baby toward a red light.

title: Fifty-One Percent
logline: Teenage Phillies prospects paint flags and their mothers' names on their spikes, until an old coordinator who learned the game barefoot calls them out.

title: Ash Glaze
place: Laurel Branch (fictional), Yancey County, North Carolina
logline: During a six-day wood firing in the Blue Ridge, an old Zen potter says the small man who loads the back of the kiln killed his parents.

title: The Brass Tray
logline: A Syrian peddler's son, left alone under a coal wagon by a prairie graveyard, wakes beside the richest man's stolen brass tray.

title: The Night Show
logline: On the last night of Frontier Days, a rancher's daughter who gave the ranch away walks her animal sanctuary's fence alone, listening to the town.

title: The Bread Truck
place: Bloomington, Indiana, to Mount Shasta, California
logline: An Indiana health-food grocer loads a bread truck with rice and drives to Mount Shasta to meet a voice he knows only from cassettes.

title: Eight Handfuls
place: Grass Valley, California, and Denver, Colorado
logline: A Cornish mine captain's daughter marries into Denver silver money and will not sit in her father-in-law's dark séance room.

title: Clean Bark
logline: The herders and the camp tender worry about a Basque herder in the Big Horns who sits alone at the edge of the aspens.

title: The Deed Reading
logline: In an all-Black Oklahoma town, a young lawyer reads land papers aloud for free, and the land men he is costing go looking for a girl.

title: Rose Sunday
place: Mission Hill and Dorchester, Boston, Massachusetts
logline: The weekend Boston's cardinal resigns, an old cartoonist who drew a kindly priest for thirty-five years sees something over Mission Hill and smiles.

title: The Hitch Ball
logline: In the farm crisis, four Bible-school friends find a way to eat well among families who cannot, with the Series on a barn radio.

title: Two Ribbons
logline: While his brigade fights in Kandahar, a retired sergeant major's handsome son stays behind and becomes the Jody of the cadences.

title: Two Strokes
logline: On their Monday off, two associate pastors of a suburban Presbyterian church argue on the seventh hole about a single blade of grass.

title: The Ear-Mark
logline: In the last year of New York slavery, a Dutch farm wife does a thing in secret on Pinkster eve and goes to church.

title: Pipe Ash
logline: Four girls from the River Raisin go up to Detroit to learn to teach, and the town inside its pickets burns.

title: The Flea-Glass
logline: In the smallpox summer, two apprentices praise three old Frenchwomen for covering their mouths, and learn whose sake the linen is for.

title: Jelly Glasses
logline: During the garbage strike, eight thirsty children sworn never to enter the chanting man's house send one boy in for water.

title: Ask On, My Son
logline: A tavern widow with an old grudge pays boys, sailors and Company slaves to follow a Jewish refugee from Recife up the Heerestraat.

title: Green Broke
logline: An old buckaroo doing time beside a prison mustang program tells a struggling young trainer how to make a gray horse quit.

title: The Cane
logline: A widowed Ramallah grocer signs everything over to his four sons, and one by one their wives show him the door.

title: The Hog Extra
place: Oakmere (fictional), a Burlington-line suburb west of Chicago, Illinois
logline: Told in a depot agent's day book: a drowsy village president, a carload of hogs, and a boy with a yellow message blank at every meal.

title: Out of the Fire
logline: A twelve-year-old who exhorted at Cane Ridge walks home at eighteen to quit, and his stepmother sits him in the good chair.

title: The Old Bull
logline: In a circus town in the Choctaw Nation, young Gujarati motel men watch an old elephant sink into the mud of Hugo Lake.

title: The Firefinder
logline: After his department's feud over a saucer of pipe ash, an English professor spends the fire season on a Montana lookout with a mule.

title: The Added Dish
place: Angel Island, San Francisco Bay, California
logline: A schoolmaster detained on Angel Island is offered the chair of the men's own association by a visitor no bolt keeps out.

title: The Yellow Cod
logline: Seven young fishermen born on one night haul in a golden cod whose breath fouls the whole meetinghouse.

title: The Gilt
logline: In the Twins' pennant summer a Watkins man walks into a hog house and finds a young sow smiling at a former Dairy Princess.

title: The Watch Chain
logline: An orphan raised in silent prayer by the last hermits of the Wissahickon sees his uncle's goldsmith case on Front Street and does not go back.

title: Correhuela
logline: Thirty old Punjabi farmers watch a countryman loaded onto the prison bus in irons, and ask a Mexican widow what could hold a man harder.

title: The Linden Branch
logline: The most beautiful bride on Cleveland's Romanian West Side crosses the street to avoid an old nun, until her husband hires fiddlers.

title: Cloud of Witnesses
logline: A rum merchant's son runs off with a rope-dancer, learns her art, and comes home to climb a sixty-foot spar.

title: The Near Bank
logline: In a drought summer, a young missionary whose well has gone dry fills his jugs at a lonely farm, and starts shaving twice.

title: Sawn Ivory
place: Shiloh Valley, St. Clair County, Illinois
logline: An eight-year-old who knows his Greek letters gives up his bed to four old scholars and sleeps across his father's doorsill.

title: Neither East nor West
logline: In the hostage-crisis winter, an Iranian student waiting by a West Virginia highway meets a countryman whose face has no worry in it.

title: Laid Over
logline: For twelve years a suburban women's club carries four questions in its minute book, until a streetcar man knows whom to ask.

title: Laurel Hell
logline: The state's escheater digs up forty-one thousand dollars in fruit jars from a miser's cabin and asks the old schoolteacher why.

title: Thirteen Kettles
logline: A Tacoma grocer feeds the whole Klondike stampede from thirteen free soup kettles, and a packer gives a blind mail carrier one spoonful of beans.

title: Singly None
logline: Five boys who mind the air doors in an Illinois coal pit quarrel over whose door is hardest, and ask the old fireman.

title: Skill and Sport
logline: A thirteen-year-old Idaho Scout with the best arm on the project tells his friend he can hit a flying goose in the eye.

title: Two Walls
logline: A boardinghouse keeper they call Koppel the Radio must keep one secret all summer: who the two quiet men in his back room are.

title: A Case of Grapefruit
logline: An old Bank Street tattooer has four months to live; his shop fills with roses, and his youngest apprentice stops coming in.

title: The Partition
logline: A house salesman on a thin winter draw lets an old friend seat him at a week of free prime rib dinners where desert lots are sold.

title: In the Boy's Name
logline: A Punjabi cotton farmer who gives away the first of everything is halfway through his dinner when an old man comes to the door.

title: Red Clay
logline: A Thai restaurant owner in an Air Force town sits down to hear her son the monk chant, and nine burglars go to work on her house.

title: Before the Blue Is Down
logline: The summer the town takes their cattle, a Hutterite colony tries each day to set down its hatred before the flax drops its petals.

title: Sifted Meal
logline: On Salt Spring Island they say a settler's son who never fidgets was born of a panther, and they have his mother's kitchen floor to prove it.

title: The Scythe
logline: A Hungarian refugee mowing ditches for wages hangs his rags and his grandfather's scythe in an oak at the edge of a Benedictine abbey.

title: Heart Mountain
logline: In a Wyoming incarceration camp, a Nisei college boy can do nothing but watch the Issei gardener who leads the Buddhist young people.

title: The Rock Spring
logline: An old clairvoyant takes a seven-year-old grape farmer's son to serve her, and sends him for water from a Saratoga spring a man has capped.

title: Come In, Saints
logline: In a new Puritan town meant only for saints, a man who has never been sure he is one greets everyone at his table as one.

title: Dit and Dah
logline: A code instructor at a secret camp teaches thirty Tibetans that everything is made of two things, and hears them repeating it.

title: Neither Bank
logline: A muddy stranger sits down by an old canoe maker's fire on the Stono and asks where a man might find the far shore.

title: The Widow's Priests
logline: A widow out of Portugal calls the children on her bench her priests, and the town's born priest climbs the stair to ask why.

title: Light Enough
logline: A ship's boy who survived the Starving Time looks at the sunset, the moon, the governor's red cloaks, and the grey widow shelling pease.

title: Hatched at Home
logline: In a Plymouth emptying out for cattle meadow, a goat-keeping Seeker tells an old Separatist widow that he alone has truly come out.

title: Brickbats
logline: In the Haymarket year, the smoking-car regulars of a commuter train watch a freethinking lawyer test a quiet bookkeeper with his fist.

title: May Wreath
logline: In the year it snowed in June, a country doctor's daybook records how he took the aunt who raised him as his only pupil.

title: The Compass Card
logline: A student nurse at an Adventist sanitarium kneels each week toward a different county, and her roommates fear she has taken up with spirits.

title: For A' That
logline: Snowed into a suburban Burns supper, a water-softener salesman with a new clan pedigree asks the old pipe major why he is not called a piper.

title: Shadow Work
place: Ocean Grove and Asbury Park, New Jersey
logline: A girl naturalist records a 'Hindoo fakir' hanging upside down at the Methodist camp-meeting gate, and a Bengali handkerchief peddler tells her about the lizard.

title: Cast Clouts
logline: A Massachusetts magistrate sent to take depositions against a widow who flies writes home to his grieving wife instead.

title: Hombre Sincero
logline: A Bay of Pigs veteran from an old Matanzas family asks the Marielito lector in Domino Park why he calls everyone sincere but him.

title: Come Round Right
logline: A dry-goods merchant's son follows a circus girl onto the road, learns her art, and comes home to stand atop the town's hickory pole.

title: Tow Strap
logline: Eleven grown suburbanites who never learned to swim stand in a lake and watch two Ford engineers settle whose Bronco is stronger.

title: Even So
logline: A preacher's wife cries out for the Second Coming every time she trips, so four preaching brothers climb to a chain gang to curse an old Sabbath-keeper.

title: The Paper Ladle
logline: On his Easter house blessings a young celibate priest comes to his own mother's door, and she sets out harissa and every word she has saved.

title: The Seed on the Needle
logline: In the summer of the Seoul spycam protests, a young woman goes to apologize to the nun her uncle wronged ten years before.

title: These Presents
logline: A Baptist elder who preaches the falling burden grabs the shirt of the man who ran from him, in a new canal lock.

title: The Feather Trees
logline: On a garage-roof plane-spotting post beside a factory disguised as a suburb, a studio head sits nights with an old barnstormer.

title: Foot Water
place: Green River bluffs, Hart County, Kentucky
logline: The woman who has kept a Green River cave for thirty years tells how she tried to drive out the praying man who sat in her door.

title: The Hickory Stick
logline: At a Mennonite burial in 1828, a smith's widow tells the dead man what she saw at a ford in the war spring of 1778.

title: Cause Undetermined
logline: An insurance claim file on four round holes in a Woodridge split-level, opened the day of a Marathi family's first shraddha.

title: No Guile
logline: The week after the grove filled with Little, the whole county decides his older brother Wayland put him out from jealousy.

title: Sinners Welcome
logline: On a church crew rebuilding after the Thomas Fire, an old carpenter calls everyone sinner, and a new volunteer starts keeping count.

title: A Sinew's Worth
logline: On a Métis buffalo hunt where theft of even a sinew is cried in camp, an orphan boy takes a fine sash off a bush.

title: The Comforters
logline: A Mexican section foreman on the Santa Fe leaves for Michoacán before the Mennonite women's promised comforters reach his boys.

title: Field Tickets
logline: A college's old bone collector, who seems to see into the ground, leaves the Badlands before a ranch wagon brings in the students' crates.

title: Thornapple Hill
logline: The last Rusyn son left at home slips away from his own wedding car toward the monastery where his brother has a new name.

title: The Cedar Moon
logline: In the seventh year of the Texas drought, a healing-tent preacher charges a dollar to touch the moon-colored light in his nephew's body.

title: Seven Winters
logline: A freedwoman carries her child from Missouri through California for seven years, waiting for ground she is willing to have him born on.

title: Honeyed Grass
logline: A rich tanner's son sings the high part at the Ephrata Cloister; his mother pays a woman from Philadelphia to bake him home.

title: The Dog's Book
logline: A foundling floated down the Shenandoah in a cooler grows rich in a Maine trail town and asks town meeting for leave to follow a dog.

title: The White Disk
logline: A casino heir brings forty men to take a lakeshore house that has no lamps, and finds its owner out watching a disk sink.

title: The Sway Pole
logline: A Molokan boy from the Flats runs off to sway atop a carnival pole, then comes home in a Packard for his mother's funeral.

title: Plain Stone
logline: Walking with her Quaker meeting through Washington Square, a gravestone letterer who once worked the high wire passes beneath a street troupe's slack wire.

title: The Fifth Skull
logline: In Naropa's first summer, a Harvard dropout who can tap a Tibetan skull cup and tell where its owner went is put to the test by a cook.

title: Thirteen Pleats
logline: A Chinatown dim sum cook comes home from a Diamond Sutra talk, walks past his wife at the window, and hands her everything.

title: The Fiftieth Buggy
logline: A militia colonel and a county seat compete to feed fifty Dunkards, until his wife orders fifty buggies and comes up one horse short.

title: Black Honey
logline: In the Texas freeze, a blind Coptic cantor sends a boy across the ice to ask the parish's proudest man for hot water.
